name: Gas Tap Hollow

stars.name: Hollow Sun
stars.notes: Late G-type star on the border of K classification. Steady output supports extensive gas giant atmospheres in the outer system.

planets.name: Intake
planets.notes: Scorched inner rock with no atmosphere. Used as a solar energy collection point--orbital mirror arrays beam power to outer system operations.

planets.name: Regulator
planets.notes: Colony world with thin breathable atmosphere, population 340,000. Administrative hub and crew rotation center for the system's gas harvesting operations.

planets.name: Reservoir
planets.notes: Massive hydrogen-helium giant and primary harvesting target. Atmospheric skimmers operate continuously in its upper cloud layers.

planets.name: Spillover
planets.notes: Secondary gas giant with higher methane content. Harvested for specialty chemical feedstocks and exotic atmospheric compounds.

planets.name: Blowoff
planets.notes: Frozen outer body with nitrogen-methane atmosphere. Serves as an emergency fuel cache and navigational marker for incoming tankers.

anomalies.name: The Pressure Front
anomalies.notes: A storm system larger than most terrestrial planets that has persisted for at least two centuries. Skimmer operations avoid its violent updrafts, but its edges yield unusually pure hydrogen.

asteroid_belts.name: Clinker Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Rocky belt containing moderate mineral deposits. Mined opportunistically for construction materials and metals needed to maintain the system's infrastructure.

stations.name: Tap Station Alpha
stations.notes: Primary atmospheric processing station. Coordinates skimmer fleets and compresses harvested gases into transportable fuel cells.

stations.name: Regulator Port
stations.notes: Main port of call for tanker traffic. Crew recreation, supply depot, and administrative offices for Gas Tap operations.

stations.name: Spillover Skimworks
stations.notes: Smaller atmospheric processing facility specializing in methane-derived chemical products and exotic gas extraction.

faction_control.notes: The Collective operates Gas Tap Hollow as one of its primary fuel production systems. Stable governance with strong union traditions among skimmer crews.

history: Surveyed in 2445 by Nimbus Fuel Collective scouts specifically seeking gas giant systems suitable for large-scale atmospheric harvesting.
Regulator colony established in 2451 as a permanent crew base; the system reached full production capacity by 2460, supplying fuel to the entire Nimbus Verge sector.

The Pressure Front megastorm on Reservoir was first charted in 2478 and has been continuously monitored since; its edges have become a prized harvesting zone for experienced skimmer pilots willing to risk the turbulence.
description: Gas Tap Hollow is a fuel production system built around two gas giants whose atmospheres supply hydrogen, helium-3, and exotic chemical compounds to the Nimbus Verge sector. The yellow-orange star Hollow Sun illuminates five worlds arranged in a configuration ideally suited to atmospheric harvesting--rocky inner planets for infrastructure, gas giants in the middle orbits for extraction, and a frozen outer marker that guides tanker convoys inward. The system's name comes from the industrial taps driven into Reservoir's atmosphere, visible as glowing trails in the planet's cloud bands.

Regulator serves as the human face of an operation that is otherwise defined by enormous scale and minimal glamour. Its 340,000 inhabitants work rotations on the skimmer fleets, process fuel at the orbital stations, or support those who do. Life here revolves around shift schedules and production quotas, softened by the Nimbus Fuel Collective's strong union culture that ensures fair wages and mandatory recreation time. Tanker traffic is steady but not heavy--the fuel cells produced here are compact and valuable, requiring fewer shipments than raw material hauling.

The Pressure Front on Reservoir is both the system's greatest hazard and its most productive zone. Experienced skimmer pilots speak of riding the storm's edges the way old sailors spoke of monsoon winds--dangerous but rewarding if you know what you're doing. The Collective officially discourages unauthorized approaches, but the purity of hydrogen harvested near the Front commands premium prices. Meanwhile, Spillover's methane-rich atmosphere yields compounds used in pharmaceutical and chemical manufacturing, giving the system a diversified output that keeps it profitable even when fuel prices dip.
